title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 6 (Act to override memorandum, articles, etc.)

content.overview: Section 6 gives the Act, and any rule or instrument made under it, overriding effect over the memorandum, articles, agreement or resolution to the extent of inconsistency.
content.glance: Section 6 gives the Act, and any rule or instrument made under it, overriding effect over the memorandum, articles, agreement or resolution to the extent of inconsistency.
content.study: Section 6 is the hierarchy rule. A company cannot contract out of the Act by a memorandum clause, article, shareholder agreement or resolution. The inconsistent portion yields; the rest of the instrument may survive. The provision also saves things done before commencement where the Act so provides, and it preserves the effect of provisions that were already repealed only to the extent the Act continues them. In a conflict between articles and a mandatory section, plead s. 6 before arguing indoor management or contractual freedom. Section 6 does not itself create a new offence; the operative section supplies the duty and consequence.

examples.title: Article vs Act
examples.body: An article allowing the board to refuse a transfer without reasons does not displace s. 58 appeal rights.

examples.title: Agreement vs Act
examples.body: A shareholders' agreement fixing quorum below the statutory floor is ineffective to that extent.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can articles legalise a prohibited loan to a director?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. To the extent the article conflicts with the Act, s. 6 prevails.
